text.p: The New York Yankees clinched their first outright division title in 16 years Wednesday, wrapping up the American League East with a 19-2 rout of the Milwaukee Brewers.
The Yankees, who earned the wild card last year and lost in the first round of the playoffs, won their clincher the same way they won the division -- building a big early lead and cruising home.

New York, which scored four runs in the first inning and 10 in the second, took first place for good on April 30, led the Orioles by 12 games on July 28 but saw the advantage dwindle to 2 1/2 games before taking two of three from the Orioles last week.

"We set out in the spring on a mission, and this is just a part of it," first-year manager Joe Torre said. "We have three more steps to go, but it's a big thrill. What helped us is the fact that we have veterans and nobody panicked."
"It's just a magnificent feeling," outfielder Bernie Williams said.
Ace David Cone (7-2), who missed four months after an aneurysm was discovered in his right shoulder, worked six solid innings.
Tino Martinez homered and drove in five runs to lead a 20-hit attack that produced the club's biggest run output in 34 years. Milwaukee's John Jaha hit his 35th homer.

The Yankees won the A.L. East in 1980 and shared the division title with Milwaukee in the strike season of 1981 and beat the Brewers in a five-game divisional playoff. The Yankees led the East in 1994 when the season was cancelled following a players' strike.
The clincher came in the first game of a doubleheader.
In the nightcap, Kenny Rogers (12-8) won his second straight start and Darryl Strawberry and Charlie Hayes drove in two runs each as the Yankees won 6-2.

In Boston, Rafael Palmeiro hit a two-run homer and Mark Parent added a three-run shot in the ninth inning as the Baltimore Orioles put the Red Sox on the brink of elimination from the American League wild-card race with a 6-2 victory.

Boston is four games behind Baltimore with four games remaining. The Orioles, eliminated from the A.L. East race before they took the field, remained 1 1/2 games ahead of Seattle in the wild-card chase.
Palmeiro's 39th homer, in the first inning off starter Tim Wakefield (14-13), gave him 142 RBI, breaking the team record set by Jim Gentile in 1961.
At California, Dave Hollins homered and drove in four runs as the Seattle Mariners routed the Angels 11-2, breaking their three-game losing streak.

The win moved the Mariners within 2 1/2 games of idle first-place Texas in the American League West. The Rangers begin a four-game series with the Angels Thursday. Baltimore is at Boston, while Seattle begins a four-game set at Oakland.
Salomon Torres (3-2) allowed two runs and seven hits over 6 1/3 innings and three relievers combined to hold the Angels to three hits over 2 2/3 scoreless innings.
Randy Velarde homered for California.
In Chicago, Mike Macfarlane hit a two-run homer and Craig Paquette added a solo shot as the Kansas City Royals dimmed the faint playoff hopes of the White Sox with an 8-2 win.
Chicago is now 2 1/2 games behind Baltimore and a game behind Seattle in the wild-card race.

Royal starter Kevin Appier (14-11) allowed a pair of runs and seven hits over six innings. Jeff Granger and Hipolito Pichardo combined to hold the White Sox to three hits over the final three innings.
Chicago starter Kevin Tapani (13-10) lasted just 2 1/3 innings, allowing four runs and four hits.
In Cleveland, Charles Nagy tossed a five-hitter and Brian Giles had three hits and two RBI as the Indians defeated the Minnesota Twins 6-3 for their fifth straight win.

The Indians, who had already clinched the Central Division, have won 15 of their last 17 games and need two more victories to become the first team since the Orioles in 1979-80 to post consecutive 100-win seasons.
Nagy (17-5) walked one and struck out five in his fifth complete game. He recorded 19 groundball outs and is 23-8 lifetime at Cleveland's Jacobs Field.

In Detroit, Ed Sprague hit a two-run homer in the top of the sixth inning to start a six-run rally and propel the Toronto Blue Jays to a 13-11 win over the Tigers, handing them their 14th straight home loss.
Julio Mosquera, a late addition to the lineup because Sandy Martinez had the flu, had four hits and drove in two runs for Toronto, which banged out 18 hits, including at least one from every starter.
